about: Labelled turns for tuning the autonomous research gate (skippy_gate).
Each case is a thing someone might actually say to Skippy, labelled with what he
research  - answering well needs current sources; getting it from memory risks
answer    - stable knowledge, arithmetic, or the user's own project. Checking it
would spend a run to be told what he already knew.
ideation  - opinion, design, banter, thinking out loud. There is no fact here to
settle, and going away to read the internet interrupts the person.
`answer` and `self_check` are what the answering model produced and then said about
itself, for tuning the confidence threshold. They are hand-written rather than
recorded from live runs, and deliberately include the two ways that layer fails: a
wrong answer given confidently (no threshold catches it) and honest modesty about an
opinion (which the empty `checkable` list is what saves us from). Replace them with
recorded ones — `python -m tests.gate_eval --live` — when there are enough real runs
to draw from; the point of keeping the set in the repo is that the threshold in
skippy_gate.py is a number somebody can re-derive rather than a number somebody felt.
